questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Firstly my focus was a country who spoke english. Secondly I wanted to go somewhere unique and somewhere I could see my self live. I have always wanted to go to Australia, so for me it was a no brainer.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think Copenhagen University and Macquarie University have been very good at providing information a long the way. If you had any questions it was clear who to contact

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Only orientation at Macquarie University if that counts.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I used flatmates and I was very lucky to live with two nice guys from Australia and England.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive but it is worth it to live in the city instead of on campus at it is in North Sydney.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't really know anything about it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The University has made a lot of videos and descriptions of all you need to do, so you can easily find all the information you need on their platform.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They has a service called 'service connect' who you could ask almost anything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I had no problems with registering

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the university webside, it really has almost all the information you need if you take the time to research a little.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I don't think the level aligned with the level we have in Denmark. Several of the courses was more BA level than MA level in my opinion.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They use more dynamic teaching with presentations and class discussions and questions in plenum. I liked that. Further you where acknowledged by the work you delivered during the semester in terms of assignments, quizzes and presentations which all counted as part of your final grade. I thought that was really nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Principles of finance
Managing finance
Financial statement analysis and modeling 
Business and global environmental change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't recommend any of them. The courses: Principles of finance, Managing finance and Financial statement analysis and modeling was kind of all a variation of Erhvervsøkonomi at UCPH and Business and global environmental change was not at all what I expected. I hoped it was very case based with a lot of focus on research and giving us some skills to combine environmental change with an economic perspective, but I feel like the professor has very low expectations for us and unfortunately used a lot of time showing us ted talk videos or something like that.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No one

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent and public transport. It was a bit unfair that some universities in Sydney gave the possibility of a student public transport card where others didn't (Macquarie didn't)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They had a global leadership program which provided a lot of activities and lectures/talks. Also cultural events. 
The school also had a fitnessclub with a pool which was really nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you live on campus I would recommend joining the fitnessclub. Otherwise the global leadership program is a good opportunity to meet some other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Sydney has a lot to offer (The Opera, Bondi beach, Harbour Bridge, the Blue mountains, Figure 8 pools, Sydney fish market). A lot of nice areas (Newtown, Surry Hills). 
In general Sydney has a lot of great food and Australia has really good and cheap coffee

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Much like at home I would say.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found that the school was very international so it was a bit hard to socialize with aussie students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No challenges.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The chill and laid back attitude.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Even though signing up for exchange is a long and though process it is all worth it and relax a bit - if you need to do something someone will let u know. And enyoy it is an amazing experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of anything

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friends I made from all over the world and the opportunity to try to live in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trying to make it as much a everyday life instead of constantly feeling you where on vacation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
